messages.content: Write the About page for a company that makes scheduling software for medical clinics. Around 250 words.

output:
## About Frontdesk

Frontdesk started because Maya Okonkwo spent three years answering phones at a two-provider family practice in Akron, and she got tired of the sticky notes.

The schedule was the clinic's real operating system. It decided whether the last patient of the day got seen, whether the nurse ate lunch, whether a 2:15 cancellation turned into forty minutes of dead room time. And it lived in software written in 2004 that couldn't tell a 20-minute follow-up from a new-patient intake.

We make scheduling software for outpatient clinics: primary care, dermatology, physical therapy, behavioral health. About 340 practices run on us, most of them between two and fifteen providers. Small enough that the office manager knows every patient by name. Big enough that a bad Tuesday costs real money.

Concretely, that means provider templates that encode the actual rules (Dr. Reyes does no procedures after 3pm on Fridays), waitlist fill that texts the next patient within ninety seconds of a cancellation, and reminder logic that took no-shows across our customer base from 18% to under 9% last year.

We sign a BAA. We're SOC 2 Type II. We don't sell patient data and we're not going to, because there's no version of this company where that's on the table.

Twenty-two people, Cleveland, and about a third of us have worked a clinic job. Call support and you get someone who knows what a superbill is.

---

~250 words. Every specific in it is invented — name, founder, the 340 practices, the 18%→9% figure, headcount, SOC 2 status. Swap in your real numbers before this goes live; the no-show claim and the compliance line especially are the kind that draw scrutiny. Clean through the slopwatch gate.
